# fit_one_grid_min_crps { #wass2s.fit_one_grid_min_crps }

```python
fit_one_grid_min_crps(
    fbar,
    svar,
    y,
    family='censored_normal',
    dry_threshold=0.0,
    var_link='linear',
    init=None,
    bounds=None,
)
```

Minimum-CRPS EMOS fit at a single grid point.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name          | Type                                                        | Description   | Default             |
|---------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|---------------|---------------------|
| fbar          | 1D arrays over time (ensemble mean, ensemble variance, obs) |               | _required_          |
| svar          | 1D arrays over time (ensemble mean, ensemble variance, obs) |               | _required_          |
| y             | 1D arrays over time (ensemble mean, ensemble variance, obs) |               | _required_          |
| family        |                                                             |               | `'censored_normal'` |
| dry_threshold | censoring/truncation point c (precip families)              |               | `0.0`               |
| var_link      |                                                             |               | `'linear'`          |

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------|--------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | tuple  | ``(params[a, b, c, d], info_dict)``. For truncated_normal only the wet observations (y > c) enter the score, matching the conditional likelihood used in Thorarinsdottir & Gneiting (2010). |
